runs.title: Christiane Amanpour: what she and CNN said
runs.prompt: CNN's chief international anchor Christiane Amanpour is leaving the network after 43 years. Find out what she said about her departure, when she will leave, and what CNN has said. Use a source that is not paywalled. Start at AP News and BBC News and work from there.
runs.answer: In a statement, Christiane Amanpour said: "After many months of thought and a few sleepless nights, I have decided to separate from CNN, my partner of 43 fantastic years!" She thanked "all the amazingly talented people I've worked with throughout this incredible journey. Especially my beloved show teams and field crews," said she looks forward to "interesting new projects down the line," vowed to keep "rooting for CNN and maintaining its history of independent journalism," and signed off with "always be truthful, not neutral." She will leave "next year" (2027) — no exact date has been given — ending a CNN career that began in 1983 as an assistant on the international news desk. CNN chairman Mark Thompson called her "one of the most trusted and beloved journalists anywhere" and said the network will "take time to celebrate her" before she departs; in a staff memo he wrote that they had discussed the decision "for some months" and that while he is "very sorry to see her go," he accepts "this is the right time for her, both personally and professionally," thanking her for "43 extraordinary years of remarkable journalism, loyalty and friendship."

runs.title: Alberta base fire: the official word
runs.prompt: Four Canadian soldiers were killed and dozens injured in a fast-moving grass fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta over the weekend of October 17-18, 2026. What happened, and what have the Canadian government and the Canadian Armed Forces officially said about the deaths and any investigation? Start at canada.ca and forces.gc.ca and work from there.
runs.answer: A fast-moving grass fire broke out inside the training area at CFB Wainwright, Alberta, on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, and swept past the base boundary; four Canadian Armed Forces members were killed and 39 people were hospitalized (the fire was declared "being held" around 10:45 pm that night). It was declared a mass-casualty incident — Edmonton's Royal Alexandra and University of Alberta hospitals went to code orange, and Alberta Health Services sent 22 ground ambulances, 2 STARS helicopters and 6 fixed-wing air ambulances, with patients also taken to Red Deer and Calgary. Officially: DND/CAF issued a statement on Oct. 18 confirming four members dead and dozens injured, saying the fire ignited within the training area and spread beyond the base boundaries and that the cause is under investigation (next-of-kin notification and family support were being prioritized). Prime Minister Mark Carney confirmed the four deaths and dozens seriously wounded at an Oct. 18 press conference, called it "a violent, fast-moving fire" and "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime," said "the nation is in mourning," and ordered flags at half-mast on all federal buildings

runs.prompt: Go to CNN's own website and pull up CNN's article about Christiane Amanpour leaving the network after 43 years. Report the headline, her key quote, and the date she will leave. If the site blocks you or the page will not load, describe exactly what happens.
runs.answer: CNN's article (by Brian Stelter, published Oct 19, 2026) is headlined "Christiane Amanpour announces she will leave CNN next June." Her key quote: "After many months of thought and a few sleepless nights, I have decided to separate from CNN, my partner of 43 fantastic years!" She also said she will always root for CNN and stay true to its independent journalism — "Remember: always be truthful, not neutral." She will sign off in June 2027: her nightly program moves to once a week in January 2027 and ends in May, with her reporting for CNN continuing through June.
